user.title: Aquarium Wavemaker
user.description: This groups your wavemaker pumps into one aquarium. First create a Toggle helper (Settings > Devices & services > Helpers > Create helper > Toggle) and pick it here as the master toggle: ON lets the schedule control the pumps, OFF stops sending and each pump keeps running its last wave. Add the integration again for a second aquarium.

data_description.name: Used to name the devices, for example 'Reef Pump 1'.
data_description.master_entity: An input_boolean helper. Each aquarium needs its own.

pump.title: Connect your first pump
pump.description: You do not pick a speed entity. Home Assistant tells your wavemaker ESP32 which wave to run by calling an ESPHome action on it (see esphome/wavemaker.yaml); the ESP32 then controls the motor itself. {found}\n\nMore pumps, schedules, followers and renaming are done in the Aquarium Wavemaker card.

data_description.name: Letters, numbers and underscores. You can change the name shown later; this id stays the same.
data_description.service: The action your ESP32 provides, named esphome.<device>_set_wave. One ESP32 has one action shared by all its pumps.
data_description.channel: Counts from 0: the first motor output in the YAML is 0, the second is 1. Pumps on the same ESP32 share the action and differ in channel.
